gloss: the right hand, the right side; (facing east) the south
summary: יָמִין is the right hand and the right side, set again and again against שְׂמֹאל the left (Gen 48:13–14; Jon 4:11). A man found his bearings facing the sunrise, so the right is also the south: “north and יָמִין, you created them” (Psa 89:13), and תֵּימָן, formed from it, is the south and the south wind, the side of the camp that set out at the second blast (Num 10:6). The right hand is the hand of strength, of blessing and of the oath, and the place at a king’s right is the place of honour; so Yahweh’s right hand is his power acting for his people (Exo 15:6), and he says to David’s lord “sit at my right hand” (Psa 110:1), which the New Testament reads of Jesus exalted. Arabic yamīn, Akkadian imnu, Ugaritic ymn and Sabaic ymn are the same word, and Arabic and Sabaic also use it for the south.

words.summary: The right hand, and the side it is on; with a verb of turning, “to the right”; and, for one facing east, the south. Of a man, the hand that does the work, bears the sword and swears; of a king, the place beside him for the one he honours; of Yahweh, his power at work.

senses.definition: The hand on the right side of the body, distinguished from the left: the hand laid on the firstborn’s head in blessing, the hand that wields a weapon, the hand of skill.

evidence.note: Joseph takes Ephraim “in his יָמִין, toward Israel’s left”, and Manasseh in his left, toward Israel’s right.
Israel stretches out his יָמִין on Ephraim’s head, the younger, and his left on Manasseh’s, crossing his hands.
Joseph is displeased that his father lays “the hand of his right” on Ephraim.
Ehud, a Benjamite, “a man bound in his right hand” (אִטֵּר יַד־יְמִינוֹ): left-handed; he draws the sword from his right thigh with his left hand (Jdg 3:21).
Seven hundred chosen Benjamites bound in the right hand, slinging stones at a hair.
Jael: her hand to the tent peg, “her יָמִין to the workmen’s hammer”.
Nineveh’s people “do not know between their יָמִין and their left”.
“If I forget you, Jerusalem, let my right hand forget”: the hand of skill.
Joab takes Amasa by the beard with his right hand to kiss him.
The bow struck from Gog’s left hand, the arrows from his right.
The worthless shepherd: a sword on his arm and on his right eye.
Nahash would put out every right eye.
“His left under my head, and his right embraces me.”
שׁוֹק הַיָּמִין, the right thigh of the peace offering, the priest’s portion: here of an animal’s right side.

senses.gloss: the right side; at the right of
senses.definition: The side on a person’s right, or on the right of a thing or place: where one stands or is set beside another, and, with “left”, both sides of him.

evidence.note: The waters were a wall to them “on their right and on their left”.
All the host of heaven standing by Yahweh on his throne, on his right and on his left.
Men stand beside Ezra on his right, others on his left.
The face of a lion on the right side of the four, an ox on the left.
Joshua the high priest before the angel of Yahweh, “and the adversary (הַשָּׂטָן) standing at his right hand to oppose him”: the place of an accuser beside the one judged.
“Let an adversary (שָׂטָן) stand at his right hand.”
Against that, Yahweh “stands at the right hand of the needy, to save him from those who judge his soul”.
“I have set Yahweh before me always; because he is at my right hand I shall not be moved”: quoted of Jesus in Act 2:25.
“Yahweh is your shade at your right hand.”
“Adonai at your right hand shatters kings in the day of his anger”: beside the king to fight for him.
A thousand at your side, ten thousand at your right hand.
“A wise man’s heart is at his right, a fool’s at his left.”

senses.gloss: to the right (in turning); right or left
senses.definition: With a verb of going or turning, the direction to the right; with “left”, any turning aside from a set way, and so from what Yahweh has commanded.

evidence.note: Abram to Lot: “If you take the left, I will go right; if the right (הַיָּמִין), I will go left.”
“That I may turn to the right or to the left.”
“We will go by the king’s highway; we will not turn aside right or left until we have passed your border.”
A narrow place, with no way to turn right or left.
“You shall be careful to do as Yahweh your God has commanded you; you shall not turn aside right or left.”
The king, that he turn not aside from the commandment, right or left.
Do according to all the law Moses commanded; turn not from it right or left.
Josiah walked in all the way of David and did not turn aside right or left.
“Do not swerve right or left; turn your foot from evil.”
“You will spread out right and left”: on every side.
“Look to the right and see: there is none who knows me.”

senses.definition: The direction on one’s right when facing the sunrise: the south, set against the north, which is on the left.

evidence.note: “צָפוֹן וְיָמִין, north and south, you created them; Tabor and Hermon shout for joy in your name.”
“Your elder sister is Samaria, who dwells at your left, and your younger sister, who dwells at your right, is Sodom”: north and south of Jerusalem.
“On the left (north) where he works I do not behold him; he turns to the יָמִין and I do not see him.”
The hill of Hachilah, “on the יָמִין of the Jeshimon”: south of it.
In the wilderness of Maon, in the Arabah, to the south of the Jeshimon.
Aroer, “on the right of the city in the midst of the valley”.

senses.gloss: right hand as strength; Yahweh’s power at work
senses.definition: The right hand as the hand of strength and action, and above all Yahweh’s right hand: his power put forth to save his people and overthrow their enemies, to uphold and to make. It stands beside his hand and his arm.

evidence.note: “Your right hand, Yahweh, glorious in power; your right hand, Yahweh, shatters the enemy.”
“You stretched out your right hand; the earth swallowed them.”
“The right hand of Yahweh does valour”, sung in the tents of the righteous as the sound of salvation.
“His right hand and his holy arm have saved for him.”
Not by their sword did they possess the land, nor did their arm save them, “but your right hand and your arm and the light of your face”.
He will answer his anointed “with the saving strength of his right hand”.
Saviour by your right hand of those who take refuge.
“Your right hand upheld me.”
“My soul clings after you; your right hand upholds me.”
“Even there your hand shall lead me, and your right hand hold me.”
“I will uphold you with the right hand of my righteousness.”
“My hand founded the earth, and my right hand spread out the heavens.”
The vine “which your right hand planted”.
“Why do you hold back your hand, your right hand?”
“He has drawn back his right hand from before the enemy.”
“The changing of the right hand of the Most High.”
“The cup of Yahweh’s right hand” comes round to the Chaldean: his judgment.
He caused his glorious arm to go at Moses’ right hand, dividing the waters.
“Then I will confess to you that your own right hand can save you.”
“Strong is your hand, high your right hand.”
Of David: “I will set his hand on the sea and his right hand on the rivers.”
Cyrus, “whose right hand I have held, to subdue nations before him”.

senses.gloss: right hand of oath and pledge
senses.definition: The right hand raised to swear or given in pledge, so that the hand stands for the oath and good faith it gives: a right hand “of falsehood” is a sworn word not kept.

evidence.note: “Yahweh has sworn by his right hand and by the arm of his strength.”
The man in linen “raised his right hand and his left hand to the heavens and swore by him who lives for ever”.

“Their right hand is full of bribes.”

senses.gloss: the place at the right hand: honour, favour
senses.definition: The place at a king’s or a father’s right hand, given to the one he honours, and the right hand as the hand of the greater blessing and of good things given.

evidence.note: Solomon rises to meet Bathsheba, sets a throne for the king’s mother, “and she sat at his right hand”.
“The queen stands at your right hand in gold of Ophir.”

“Let your hand be on the man of your right hand, on the son of man whom you made strong for yourself.”
“Put your right hand on his head”: the right hand for the firstborn’s greater blessing.
“Pleasures at your right hand for ever.”
Wisdom: length of days in her right hand, riches and honour in her left.
“Your right hand is full of righteousness.”
“You hold my right hand”: the hand by which Yahweh holds the one he keeps.

senses.gloss: right (side of a building), the south side
senses.definition: The right side of the temple or its court, which, as the house faced east, is the south side.

evidence.note: “The sea he set on the right shoulder of the house, eastward, toward the south (נֶגֶב).”

words.summary: A noun formed from the root with prefixed ת: the right-hand quarter, the south. It marks the south side of the Dwelling and its court, the camps that lay south of it (Num 2:10; 10:6), the southern border of the land, and the south wind. Teman, the region and clan of Edom, has the same spelling; it is a name and is not entered here.

senses.definition: The southern quarter, and, with ה of direction (תֵּימָנָה), toward the south: of the side of the Dwelling, of the camps, of borders, and as one of the four quarters.

evidence.note: “When you blow a second alarm, the camps that lie תֵּימָנָה shall set out”: after the east camps (Num 10:5), the south ones, Reuben’s banner (Num 10:18).
“The banner of the camp of Reuben shall be תֵּימָנָה by their hosts.”
The families of Kohath camp on the side of the Dwelling תֵּימָנָה.
Twenty boards “for the side נֶגְבָּה תֵימָנָה”: Negev-ward, southward, the two words together.
The lampstand opposite the table “on the side of the Dwelling תֵּימָנָה, and the table you shall put on the north (צָפוֹן) side”.
From Pisgah Moses looks “westward and northward and תֵימָנָה and eastward”: the four quarters.
“I will say to the north, Give up, and to the תֵימָן, Do not hold back; bring my sons from afar.”

“The south side, southward (נֶגֶב תֵּימָנָה)”, from Tamar to the waters of Meribah-Kadesh.

The hawk stretches its wings toward the south.
“God came from תֵּימָן, the Holy One from Mount Paran”: the south, or Edom’s Teman, as Paran beside it suggests.

senses.definition: The wind from the south, set beside the east wind and the north wind.

“Awake, north wind, and come, תֵימָן; blow on my garden.”

words.gloss: (hiphil) go to the right; use the right hand
words.summary: A verb made from יָמִין, found only in the hiphil and always set against its fellow from שְׂמֹאל (הִשְׂמִיל, “go left”). Isa 30:21 spells it with א, תַאֲמִינוּ, though it is not the verb אָמַן “be firm”.

“None can turn to the right or to the left (לְהֵמִין וּלְהַשְׂמִיל) from anything my lord the king has said.”
To the sword: “Go right (הֵימִנִי), set yourself, go left, wherever your edge is appointed.”

doctrine.statement: Scripture speaks of Yahweh’s right hand where it speaks of his power put forth: it shattered the enemy at the sea and the earth swallowed them (Exo 15:6, 12); it spread out the heavens (Isa 48:13); it planted the vine Israel (Psa 80:16); it saves and upholds (Psa 98:1; 63:9; Isa 41:10). Israel did not win the land by its own sword or arm, “but your right hand and your arm and the light of your face, because you delighted in them” (Psa 44:4), and in the tents of the righteous the song is “the right hand of Yahweh does valour” (Psa 118:15–16). When he withdraws it, the enemy prevails (Lam 2:3; Psa 74:11). From the verses: what his people have, of deliverance, land and strength, they have by his doing and not their own.

The place at a king’s right hand is given to the one he honours beside him: Solomon sets his mother there (1Ki 2:19), and the queen stands there (Psa 45:10). In Psa 110:1 Yahweh says to David’s lord (אֲדֹנִי), “Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool”, and Psa 80:18 prays for “the man of your right hand, the son of man whom you made strong for yourself”. Jesus asks how David’s son can be David’s lord (Mat 22:41–45), and tells the council that they will see the Son of man sitting at the right hand of power and coming on the clouds (Mat 26:64; Dan 7:13). Peter says that David did not ascend into the heavens, but God raised Jesus, exalted him by his right hand, and made him both lord and Christ (Act 2:32–36); Hebrews says that he sat down at God’s right hand and from then on waits until his enemies are made his footstool (Heb 10:12–13), and Paul that he must reign until all enemies are under his feet, and then the Son himself will be subject to the Father (1Co 15:25–28). From the verses: the one at the right hand is a man, David’s son, raised and exalted by God, distinct from Yahweh who seats him there and subdues his enemies for him; his sitting there lasts “until”, and ends in his coming to reign.

Israel is told to do as Yahweh commanded and “not turn aside right or left” (Deu 5:32; 28:14); the king is to read the law all his days, that he not turn from the commandment right or left (Deu 17:19–20); Joshua is to keep all the law and not turn from it right or left, that he may prosper (Jos 1:7); and Josiah is commended because he did not (2Ki 22:2). The way is the commandment, and any step off it, to either side, is a departure. Isaiah promises a word from behind, “This is the way, walk in it”, when they would turn right or left (Isa 30:21), and Proverbs joins not swerving with turning the foot from evil (Pro 4:27).
